core_territory: Laos (all 17 provinces + Vientiane Prefecture) — per the survey, 'Laos IS Zomia rather than merely containing it' (§3.4); on the high end of the survey's cited range, 46.8% of the population sits in the Lao Theung (midland) and Lao Sung (highland) elevation tiers.
domain_territory: ⚠️ UPDATED 2026-09-26, evidence pass (not yet folded into the survey text itself — see that file's own dated addendum). Myanmar: Shan, Kachin (2,153,483), Chin (373,023), Kayah/Karenni (296,901) and Kayin/Karen (1,502,774) States — extension beyond Shan alone now evidence-backed: Scott's own stated Zomia scope is upland Burma generally, not Shan specifically, and all four are substantially highland terrain (Kachin, Chin and Karenni Hills; Karen highlands). Thailand: NINE Upper Northern provinces, Tak added — Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Mae Hong Son, Nan, Phayao, Phrae, Lampang, Lamphun, Tak. Verified against the Wikipedia 'Nationality, religion, and language' provincial dataset (1990/2000 hill-tribe-speaker shares): Mae Hong Son (51.1%→63.0%) and Tak (18.1%→24.3%) are the two real highland cores; Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai and Nan show strong 2000 growth (12.5%, 13.4%, 10.5%); Lampang (0.8%→1.0%) and Phrae (1.0%→1.9%) are the weakest members of the list and worth flagging as marginal rather than dropping outright. Vietnam: Lai Châu, Điện Biên, Sơn La, Cao Bằng, Lạng Sơn, Lào Cai, Tuyên Quang — all seven confirmed ethnic-minority-majority by named-group census percentages (e.g. Lai Châu: Kinh only 15.91%; Điện Biên: Kinh 17.38%; Sơn La: Kinh 16.26%; Cao Bằng: Kinh 5.12%; Lạng Sơn: Kinh 16.09%). The 2025-merger provinces check out on both halves: Lào Cai (new) = old Lào Cai + Yên Bái, and Tuyên Quang (new) = old Tuyên Quang + Hà Giang — Hà Giang and Yên Bái are themselves strongly ethnic-minority-majority (Hà Giang: Kinh only 12.32%), so the merger does not dilute either case. Quảng Ninh's exclusion stands, unexamined this pass. ⚠️ An earlier draft of this row also carried Thái Nguyên, Phú Thọ and Vietnam's Central Highlands (Quảng Ngãi, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk, Lâm Đồng) — those five are NOT carried forward here: the 2026-09-26 evidence pass only checked and confirmed the seven provinces named above, and never examined the Central Highlands' own ethnic-minority case (a real highland region, but historically treated as distinct from Scott's mainland-massif Zomia rather than folded into it). Flagged for a future look, not silently dropped.

The survey's own conclusion: treat Zomia descriptively (ungoverned highland ground, whoever's people live there) rather than as a settled anthropological claim. Draw accordingly — this sphere marks terrain and demography, not a political argument. Whether to actually extend the Myanmar domain to all four states or keep Shan-only remains the author's call — this pass only strengthens the evidence for the option, it doesn't choose it.

core_territory: The Deep South (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat — independent nation as of 2026-09-26, formerly Thailand's own 'Deep South'), 77% Muslim, where Patani Malay is the majority language. Historically the Sultanate of Patani (15th–18th century), a Malay-Muslim polity split from the rest of the Malay world by the colonial-era Anglo-Siamese border, not by any cultural or linguistic line.
domain_territory: Named but out of scope on THIS map, label only — do not draw territory: Malaysia's Kelantan and Terengganu, on the Maritime Southeast Asia companion map. Not a loose cultural-affinity claim: 'Kelantan-Pattani Malay' is a real, named linguistic classification (Glottolog) spoken continuously across Pattani/Yala/Narathiwat and Kelantan/Terengganu (Besut and Setiu districts specifically) — native speakers on both sides of the border 'often cannot differentiate' each other's speech.

notes: ⚠️ NOT the same connection as Kedah/Perlis's own high Muslim share (78.5%/87.8%) — corrected 2026-09-26: the real distinction is linguistic, not a difference in Siamese-era status (the 1909 Anglo-Siamese Treaty transferred all four states — Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu alike — from Siam to Britain, so that treaty is not what separates them). Kedah and Perlis speak Kedah Malay, a different dialect from Kelantan/Terengganu's shared Kelantan-Pattani Malay and its Patani sultanate history. Flagged as a second, distinct, not-yet-built connection, not folded into this sphere. There is also a real, current, active insurgency in Thailand's Deep South (7,700+ deaths since 2004, martial law since 2005, a 2024 peace roadmap already deteriorating as of 2026) — this sphere marks the ethnolinguistic continuity, not a political claim on it; see the frameworks survey for whether/how to note the conflict itself.
